system_overview: This specification models a consensus algorithm that can reach agreement in one communication step under favorable conditions, based on the algorithm in Figure 1 of Brasileiro et al.'s 2001 paper. The protocol operates in an asynchronous distributed system with crash failures. If enough processes propose the same value, consensus is achieved in a single round; otherwise, processes fall back to an underlying consensus protocol.
actors_and_components: The system consists of N processes that communicate by message passing. Processes may crash (up to F actual faults, bounded by T maximum tolerated faults). The protocol requires 3T less than N. Crashed processes stop sending and receiving messages but do not behave maliciously. Each process proposes a value from a finite set of possible values.
state_variables: The system tracks: the control location of each process (proposing, deciding, calling underlying consensus, crashed, or done), each process's current preferred value, each process's decision value (initially a special bottom value indicating no decision), the set of all broadcast messages (both proposal and decision messages), the set of messages received by each process. Messages carry a type (proposal or decision), a value, and a sender identifier.
initial_state: Initially, every process is in the proposing state and has a randomly chosen proposed value from the value set. No process has decided (all decision values are bottom). No messages have been sent and no messages have been received.
actions: The protocol operates as follows: (1) A process may crash if the number of non-crashed processes still exceeds the fault bound, transitioning to the crashed state. (2) A process may receive a message from the set of broadcast messages that it has not yet received. (3) In the propose phase, a process broadcasts a proposal message containing its preferred value and moves to the deciding phase. (4) In the deciding phase, once a process has received proposal messages from at least N-T distinct senders: (a) if all received proposals carry the same value, the process decides that value, broadcasts a decision message, and finishes; (b) if some value appears in at least N-2T of the received proposals, the process adopts that value as its new preferred value and falls back to the underlying consensus; (c) otherwise the process falls back to underlying consensus with its current preferred value unchanged. (5) If a process receives a decision message from any other process (regardless of its current phase, as long as it has not finished or crashed), it adopts that decision value, broadcasts a decision message, and finishes. (6) Processes that have finished or fallen back to underlying consensus may take a no-op step to avoid deadlock.
safety_properties: Validity: if a process decides a value, that value was proposed by some process. Agreement: no two processes decide different values. Additionally, if any process decided a value and another process falls back to underlying consensus, the fallback process's preferred value equals the decided value. Weak agreement: no two decided processes have different decision values (without the fallback constraint).
liveness_properties: Termination: eventually every process either crashes, finishes with a decision, or falls back to the underlying consensus protocol.
model_bounds: For model checking: N=4, T=1, F=1, with a value set of two distinct values and a special bottom value for undecided processes.
additional_assumptions: Weak fairness is assumed on receiving, proposing, the core decision logic, and processing decision messages from other processes. The specification requires 3T less than N, 0 at most F at most T, and N greater than 0. The protocol models only the one-step algorithm itself without the underlying consensus sub-protocol. Inductive strengthening invariants are included for verification support.
